hints.title: Stored Procedure Parameter Filtering
hints.text: Filter Purchases where time_stamp is between startDate and endDate and amount is at least minAmount.

hints.title: Procedure Query Body
hints.text: Encapsulate the query inside the procedure definition.

hints.title: MySQL Stored Procedure Formulation
hints.text:
```sql
CREATE PROCEDURE getUserIDs(startDate DATE, endDate DATE, minAmount INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT DISTINCT user_id
    FROM Purchases
    WHERE time_stamp BETWEEN startDate AND endDate
      AND amount >= minAmount
    ORDER BY user_id;
END
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) for sorting distinct users
complexity.notes: Filtering and distinct sorting on qualifying purchase records.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Failing to deduplicate user_id produces redundant rows for users with multiple matching transactions.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Output table contains unique qualifying user IDs.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate writes clean stored procedure with BETWEEN predicate.

solutions.approach: PostgreSQL Stored Procedure with Filtered Distinct User Selection
solutions.code:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION getUserIDs(startDate DATE, endDate DATE, minAmount INT)
RETURNS TABLE(user_id INT) AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT DISTINCT p.user_id
    FROM Purchases p
    WHERE p.time_stamp BETWEEN startDate AND endDate
      AND p.amount >= minAmount
    ORDER BY p.user_id;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
